en: *Oṃ.* (Then enters Laṅkā, overwhelmed with grief. Laṅkā (with lamentation): Alas, Great King Daśagrīva, you who were dallying in the reception of the Fortune of the Three Worlds! Alas, you whose stubborn staff-like arms were capable of resisting the entire host of Rākṣasas! Alas, you whose lotus-face was innocent and blooming through the worship of the pair of feet of the Lord of Beasts (Śiva)! Alas, the preeminent son of Kekasī! Alas, you who are affectionate toward your kinsmen! Where am I to see you? Alas, Prince Kumbhakarṇa! Alas, my dear Meghanāda! Where are you? Give me an answer!
(Looking around: Why does no one speak?
(Looking upward: Alas! O wicked plaything of fate, why has it come to this? Or rather, what blame can there be here for your honor? It is one's own evil conduct that thus turns into misfortune.
(Thus she weeps compassionately.
(Then Alakā enters.

Alakā: Oh, how strange! What is this unprecedented ripening of destiny for the Lord of the Rākṣasas? For even such a vast creation of Rākṣasas has, in a mere moment, been reduced to nothing but Vibhīṣaṇa.
(Miming the hearing of a sound; walking about. What? Is my younger sister in Laṅkā, distressed by the fresh agony of separation from her husband, crying out?
(Approaching. Sister, take heart, take heart!
Lanka! (Reflecting) Where is my sister Alaka?
Alakā: Sister, take heart, take heart! Such indeed is the course of worldly existence.

Lakṣmaṇa: O elder sister, from where can I find any hope? I have become one for whom only young women remain. However, it is heard that Prince Vibhīṣaṇa alone remains as the thread of our lineage; yet, due to my own ill fortune and lack of merit, even he serves only as a target for the enemy.
Alakā: O sister, do not speak thus! That faction of enemies is certainly not ours.
Lanka! Where is it?
Alakā—He who was its enemy has departed, and that [enmity] has vanished. But now, the son of Daśaratha, whose alliance is renowned for protecting the three worlds, is our natural friend.
Lanka!
(Sighing) How can he be even such as this?
Alakā is exactly like this.
Lanka! Where has our Master become so transformed?
Alaka: Even without further inquiry, why do you speak thus? Listen:

while this ornament of Raghu’s lineage has entered the Daṇḍaka forest at his father’s command, accompanied only by his brother and mother, all that was fitting for him as the subduer of the Rākṣasas has been performed; this is the complete fruition of that deed. (1)
Lakṣmaṇa: Huṃ! But how have you arrived here at such a time?

Alakā: Pay attention. It is said that I have been dispatched by my half-brother, the descendant of Pulastya, after he learned this news from Citraratha, the King of the Gandharvas; I am sent to inform our remaining kinsmen, to witness the consecration of Vibhīṣaṇa in Laṅkā, and to provide instructions for the presentation of the Puṣpaka—the sovereign celestial chariot seized from Rāvaṇa—to the noble Rāma.
Lakṣmaṇa: Oh! How is it that even the venerable Paśupati’s friend, the lord of the Nidhānas himself, attends upon Rāmabhadra in this manner?
Alakā: Oh, what wonder is there in this?

For this is the truth: he is the ancient Puruṣa who partakes in the ultimate reality; indeed, this very Prakṛti, divided into three forms, has descended by her own power to protect the virtuous on earth. (2)
Lanka! Why was this not perceived by our lord, the leader of the Rākṣasas?
Alakā: O simple one! By the power of the curse, he has indeed fainted into a state of delusion; he is not at fault.
(Offstage, a tumultuous noise. Both listen with agitation. (Again offstage:
"Pay heed, O beings who roam the three worlds!
Here is Vṛddhaśravas himself, accompanied by the Vasus, Arka, and Rudras; he personally congratulates this virtuous woman, saying, 'Excellent! Excellent!'"
O best of the Raghus, honor Sītā’s state of being, which is pure due to her emergence from entering the fire and her abiding in existence.

Alakā: How is it that even these denizens of heaven, in order to dispel the rumors arising from the suspicion that she might have been compelled to dwell in the house of the Ten-necked one, celebrate the Queen Sītā for having entered and emerged from the fire? Alas!
This light consisting of devotion to her husband is being purified by another light!
This is a marvel; or rather, it is simply following the natural course of the world. (4)
(Miming the hearing of a sound) Laṅkā: How is it that the sounds of auspicious trumpets are being heard?
Alakā.

(Looking toward the dressing room: How is it that Vibhīṣaṇa, whose auspicious consecration has been performed by the celestial nymphs and hosts of divine sages who descended to express their approval of Sītā’s purification, approaches Rāmabhadra with the Puṣpaka chariot at his head? Come then; let us satisfy our eyes by beholding this high-souled one, whose conduct is honored by its innate majesty.
(Thus, having walked about, they exit. //The Mixed Interlude.//
(Then enters Rāma, accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, with Hanumān and Sugrīva at his side.
Rāma: Why does Vibhīṣaṇa delay?

(Then enters Vibhīṣaṇa, preceded by the Puṣpaka chariot. Vibhīṣaṇa: Indeed, the command of the noble Rāma has been carried out by me. For thus it is: following Mātali, who was honored [by us], the women of the celestial realm—whose cheeks bear the marks of scars from the constant flow of tears, whose golden bracelets are slipping off, who wear a single braid of hair, and whose garments are soiled from rolling upon the ground—are now departing with smiles, having been released. 5.
(Approaching: Victory, victory to Rāmabhadra! Your Majesty, this command has indeed been fulfilled to its conclusion.
Now these prisons are adorned with golden chains that are visible and have fallen [upon them], as if they were female captives. (6)
And this is that king of celestial chariots named Puṣpaka; its movement is unimpeded, and it always acts in accordance with the will of its master, who exercises control over its course. //7//
Rāma: Well done, Lord of Laṅkā! Well done! You have accomplished it perfectly.
(To Sugrīva: Friend Vaikartana, what remains here to be done?

Sugrīva: This thorn of the three worlds has been uprooted, and this insult—whose greatness was bolstered by his exceedingly arrogant staff-like arms—has likewise been pacified for the Goddess; thus, the agreement has been fulfilled here through the consecration of the upright Vibhīṣaṇa. (8)

But now, Prince Bharata is reportedly distressed, having received specific news regarding Hanumān as he returns with Mount Droṇa; let a messenger of the Wind-god be dispatched to him, and let the king of celestial chariots be adorned by you yourself.
Rāma: Whatever is pleasing to my dear friend.
(Thus having done so, they all mime ascending the celestial chariot.
Sītā:
(Aside, toward Lakṣmaṇa: Where are we headed now?
Lakṣmaṇa: O Queen, toward Ayodhyā, the royal capital of the Raghu dynasty.
Sītā: Has that period of dwelling in the forest indeed come to an end?
Lakṣmaṇa: O Queen, it was indeed this very day.
(All observe the movement of the celestial chariot.
Sītā:
(With wonder) Noble Lord, what are these surrounding regions that appear from afar with their distinct boundaries clearly defined and their dark-blue nature spreading forth?
Rāma:
(With a smile) O Queen, these are not the outskirts of the earth; rather, this is indeed the first watery form of that [Lord] who possesses eight manifestations.
It is called the "Ocean" by men, for its depth of self is truly immeasurable. (9)

Sītā: It is heard through the tradition of the elders that this was built by our eldest fathers-in-law; yet, in the midst of this, why is there seen this white cloth-like thing stretched out far over the ground covered with fresh grass?

Lakṣmaṇa: My Queen, this new bridge—its greatness to be venerated until the end of the aeon—is seen by the world like a pillar of glory for the noble conduct of the King, constructed in the ocean by the leaders of the tree-dwellers who, full of zeal and curiosity, brought stones from the peaks of the great mountains at the ends of the quarters and had it built under his command. (10)
Rāma:

(Pointing with his finger) My child, do you recognize these regions of the earth, where clusters of cool groves are darkened by the meeting shadows of *tamāla* trees, and which receive the floods of waterfalls cascading down from the slopes of the lofty peaks of the clear Malaya mountains? 11.
Lakṣmaṇa: Noble brother, these are indeed those very waters. Not very far from here lies that ancient cavern.
When the quarters of the sky are shattered by thunderclaps, and when the vast, cloudless firmament repeatedly whirls with the roar of those peals due to the force of a fierce wind;
when the night, having entered the blinding darkness that strikes down the trees, was spent there amidst the falling torrents of water that rendered the trees mere hollows of sap.
Sītā:
(To herself) Oh, what a tragedy! How is it that even these two noble souls have been brought to such a state by wicked fate, through me, so unfortunate?

Vibhīṣaṇa: O Lord Rāmabhadra, these lands on the banks of the Kāverī are indeed visible. On the borders of the mountains surrounding them, various hermitages are discernible, their grounds thickened by groves of areca palms rejoicing in the cascading streams of *kuvalayāmoda* wine; there dwell sages who have realized Brahman through steady austerity and Vedic study, and who stand as witnesses to the endurance of the world-cycle. (13)
For not very far away, it is said, in the precincts adorned by Lopāmudrā toward the west, the light born of the jar (Agastya) shines forth.
Rāma: How is it that we have already passed the hermitage of Agastya?
By his playful deeds, this ocean was indeed turned into a desert; this Vindhya mountain abandoned its swelling pride and its vain, haughty sport;
and Vātāpi dissolved away while remaining within the fire of his stomach.
Or rather, may that Sage, whose self is unperceived, be the object of those words which are nourished by truth. //14//
Therefore, those great souls, whose power is immeasurable and who are witnesses to the inner self of the universe, are not to be venerated by anyone at all.
(All do so.
(In the sky:
Rule your subjects along with your younger brother; may your fame endure until the end of the aeon.
May even the mere utterance of the name "Rāma" lead me to immortality. //15//
Rāma: (Listening) What? Has the one who bows before great sages been so highly favored by an incorporeal voice?
(The others applaud.

Vibhīṣaṇa: O Lord Rāmabhadra, these are those very grounds on the outskirts of Lake Pampā, where even though they have been experienced for a long time, these tokens forcibly draw the eye. For instance:

there stands that grove of old *tāla* trees, shimmering before us, pierced by a single arrow; and there Vālin himself, for a moment, experienced the state of being a "play-monkey" here with a multitude of shafts.

For here, out of curiosity, the son of Sumitrā previously cast down a heap of bones with a kick; and in this very place, Kābandha was seen by you, as was the upper garment of the Queen, [all] while Hanumān looked on.
Sītā:
(To herself) What indeed? Has my husband seen my upper garment in the hands of Hanumān?
Rāma:

(With remembrance) O Queen! At that time, as you were being carried away in a state of agitation, we first obtained a token of recognition: your upper garment, from which the name of Anasūyā had slipped away.
To our eyes it was like the radiance of the autumnal moon, and upon our bodies it was like a shower of camphor powder.
At that time, it is said, even within his own heart there was the sprinkling of a jar of thick nectar as soon as he was seen. //17//
(Sītā acts out bashfulness at being adorned.
Lakṣmaṇa:
Noble brother, it is said that the king of vultures was a friend of our father; why do you suddenly pursue that wicked creature?
Having abandoned his body, worn out by old age, he took up a new body of glory. //18//
Sītā:
(To herself) How is it that, on my account, such a distinguished state [of distress] is observed even among those of such great nobility?
Sugrīva: My Lord, it seems these borders of Daṇḍaka are being transgressed;
for there, Triśiras, Khara, and Dūṣaṇa, along with their followers, have gone off somewhere, desiring to cut off the ears, noses, and lips of your sister. (19)
Sītā:
(Trembling) Alas! Why are those very same Rākṣasas being heard of once again?

Rāma: Queen, enough with this apprehension; only the name remains. Indeed, from the twang of the bow alone of Saumitri, the destruction of the Rākṣasas occurs, just as that of elephants follows the roar of a lion. (20)
(Observing) Why is the movement of this king of celestial chariots as if it were otherwise?

Vibhīṣaṇa said: "O Lord, this mountain Sahya is indeed exceedingly high; it is said that one must pass beyond it to reach Āryāvarta. To cross over it, even this proximity to the middle world [the atmosphere] seems to yield somewhat."
Lakṣmaṇa: It is said that the world must be seen as marked by the middle term "Supreme Person" (uttama-puruṣa).
(All observe the speed of the upward flight.
Rāma: (Observing; with astonishment.)

He who is the foundation of our ancestral lineage, the god himself, the treasury of splendors, the essence of the three Vedas incarnate—this Vivasvat has drawn near by ascending the Puṣpaka chariot. (21)
(All bow down in the *kapotaka* posture.
Sītā:
(Looking up intently) Oh! Why is it that even though it is day, this appears like a circle of stars?

Rāma: O Queen, this is indeed the circle of stars; it is said that during the day it is not seen by those whose vision is struck by the rays of the sun due to extreme distance, as it is cast aside from its ascent into the celestial chariot.
Sītā:
(With curiosity) Why do they appear like flowers in full bloom in the garden of the sky?
Rāma: (Looking all around) How is it that the world now seems as if its cardinal directions cannot be distinguished? For:
The terrestrial features are clearly not being perceived due to the great distance.
Furthermore, these atmospheric [beings] appear similar on all sides. //22//
Sugrīva: O Lord, having been brought under my influence by my brother’s affection, I have come here while wandering at will across the ends of the earth. For instance:
these two mountains, the Eastern and Western Peaks, within whose embrace the moon and the sun pass fearlessly and with full confidence during their childhood and old age [respectively]. (23)
"Pay heed to this, O Lord:
these two mountains, Kailāsa and Añjana, are equal in height and circumference;
are they not the breasts of the Earth, now rendered fragrant with the application of sandalwood and musk? (24)
On this side is this mountain of gold; on the other side is this mountain Gandhamādana with its peaks scraping the clouds. Beyond that lie regions inaccessible to those such as myself.

Rāma: (Looking all around; with agitation and wonder) How is it that in a single moment the entire world has come within the range of my vision? And yet, the manner of this creation’s existence is beyond comprehension!
Sītā: Oh! What is this? It appears to be something never seen before, quite unlike anything else; it is neither a human nor an animal.
Rāma: O Queen, this is a pair of Kinnaras with horse-like faces. Generally, it is in these very regions that such beings are most commonly found.
Vibhīṣaṇa: How is it that he approaches right before us? He must likely be one who carries out the commands of the Lord of Alakā.

(Offstage: O Lord Rāmabhadra, jewel of the Solar dynasty! We had set out for Sāketa at the command of the Lord of Ekapiṅgācala to offer hymns of praise to you; however, by the ripening of our past merits, we have come within the range of your vision even here on the way. Thus, even this dependence upon his command leads to great benefit, in that we directly perceive the splendor of the Ancient Person himself, residing in the form of an individual incarnation.
(Thus, having circumambulated [the stage], they pay homage. (Everyone gazes intently. (Again, behind the scenes:)
O Kinnara!
O you who are affectionate toward those in distress; O sole kinsman of the people of the world; O wise Rāmacandra, the lotus-pool for the swans of the learned!
May your fame be enjoyed for a thousand autumns by the cakora-birds of the virtuous, who are themselves devoid of the conditions of birth and other worldly phenomena. 25.
Right there are the Kinnarīs;

as far as this circle of the earth upon the head of the lord of serpents, and as far as the sky variegated by the hosts of planets—O Vaidehī, so long shall your stainless and meritorious fame be sung throughout the worlds by those of noble conduct. 26.
(The couple act out bashfulness.
The others: "What is dear, what is dear to us!"

Rāma: O Lord of Laṅkā, I surmise that our long wandering here has caused you some inconvenience; therefore, it would be better for us to depart from here in the presence of the inhabitants of the middle world.
Vibhīṣaṇa:
O Lord, these are the purifying foothills of Gaurī’s father (the Himalayas), their rocks washed by the celestial river, radiant with fragments of camphor, and bearing tattered birch bark;

there, the naturally sweet and gentle splendor of those knowers of Brahman awakens—those who delight in the science of the self and have dispelled the darkness of delusion through the perception of reality. 27.
Lakṣmaṇa: Noble brother, why is it that these regions of the earth, though previously so familiar, cannot bear to be perceived by my eyes as if they were foreign lands?
Rāma:

(Observing; with an outburst of memory) Dear child, these are indeed those very grounds of the penance grove, whose borders were sanctified by the movements of our venerable preceptor Kauśika’s feet. It was here that we two, who were cherished by our preceptors as they experienced the joy of various nectarian conversations with the illustrious disciple of Yājñavalkya—the second lord of Videha—indulged in the frolics appropriate for our childhood.
Sītā:
(To herself) It is said that he is my younger brother.
(Thus he gazes around with longing.
Rāma: O Lord of Laṅkā, it is not appropriate at this time to ascend a celestial chariot in these precincts purified by the dust of the lotus-feet of your preceptor.
(Offstage: Ho, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa! That venerable disciple of Kṛśāśva commands you both.
Both:
(Having directed the presiding deity of the celestial chariot by a gesture to remain motionless: We are attentive.
(Again, behind the scenes: Go to the city as you are; do not delay along the way.
The light that is the companion of Arundhatī awaits you both. (28)
I too, intent on attending to my third mealtime, shall arrive in just two muhūrtas.
Both: As our preceptors command.
(They both board the celestial chariot again.

Rāma: Oh, how even these great souls are dependent on affection! For, though their time is divided into portions for the practice of austerity and sacred study by virtue of their greatness, they still insist on coming here. Or rather, this is only fitting; since they are of a gentle nature and dependent on compassion, what need have they for the deer and trees in the penance grove, let alone for humans? Moreover, our birth in the house of kings of the Solar dynasty is merely incidental;
it is from these great souls that we derive our primary refinement, consisting chiefly of knowledge in the use of weapons and missiles. (29)
The others, as Rāmabhadra has said:
Vibhīṣaṇa: (Looking) Why is it that, all of a sudden, the quarters of the sky are being shrouded by the dust of the earth as if by veils of mist?
(All look on with astonishment. Rāma:
(Reflecting) I suspect that Bharata, having learned of our movements from the son of the Wind-god, is coming forth to meet me with his army.

(Entering, Hanumān bows down, touching his feet to the lotus-like feet of the King. My Lord, Bharata has been standing for a long time meditating upon some internal event of your own; now, having received this news from me, he approaches accompanied by his kinsmen, his hair matted and wearing bark garments, repeatedly tasting the nectar-like power of the name "Rāma," and overwhelmed with joy. (30)
Rāma:
(With joy) Oh! Having obtained the long-standing friendship of the noble one, we stand above all joys.
Lakṣmaṇa: (With eagerness) Friend Māruti, where is the noble one?
Hanumān: Among these five or six who are at the head of the army, that great-souled one who is the leader in their midst along with his younger brother is Bharata.
(Lakṣmaṇa gazes.
Sītā:
(Observing) How is it that he appears quite different?
Vibhīṣaṇa: O King of Chariots! Let these noble beings experience mutual joy for a long time through the sight of their kinsmen, embraces, greetings, and so forth; therefore, pause for a moment.
(All act out descending from their celestial chariots.
Then enter Bharata and Śatrughna, surrounded by several principal attendants.
Rāma:

(Raising up Bharata, who has fallen at his feet with impetuosity: "Come, come, my child! Your touch, rough as the quivering stalk of a lotus in its heart, brings about an experience like the direct realization of the bliss of Brahman. (31)

(Thus, having embraced him fervently, he lets him go. Lakṣmaṇa embraces Bharata while prostrating at his feet. Śatrughna pays homage to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. Both: Observe the established traditions of your lineage.
(Bharata and Śatrughna prostrate themselves before Sītā like a staff.
Sītā: O princes, may you be devoted to your elder brothers.
Rāma: Dear sons Bharata and Śatrughna, this lord of monkeys has become our boat in the ocean of calamity; and this lord of Laṅkā is a friend devoted to righteousness and welfare. (32)
Embrace it.
(Thus he points out Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa.
(Bharata and Śatrughna embrace them both and treat one another as is appropriate.

Bharata: Noble brother, our family preceptor, the venerable son of Mitrāvaruṇa, having prepared all the requisites for the consecration in the lion-throne chamber, awaits you. As you command, noble brother.
Rāma: (To himself) The feet of Viśvāmitra must be awaited. And that venerable son of Mitrāvaruṇa commands thus: "Let it be; I shall act in accordance with the occasion."
(Aloud: As the family preceptor commands.
(All walk about.
(Then enter Vasiṣṭha with the wives of Daśaratha, and Arundhatī walking beside him. Vasiṣṭha:
(To himself:

"He is the fertile field of forbearance, a mine for the multitude of jewel-like virtues, the embodied fruition of the merit of all living beings who have sought refuge, and a garden of compassion—Rāma. 'Let him be drunk in with our eyes here outside! Out of such joy, we are indeed turning even above him. (33)
Let it be so; nevertheless, one must conform to the ways of the world.
(Aloud: Daughters-in-law Kausalyā and Sumitrā!
"Both of you, let the family preceptor be informed."
Vasiṣṭha: By good fortune, you two have returned with your daughter unharmed.
Both of these are due to the power of your blessings.
Arundhatī:
(Looking at Kaikeyī) My child Kaikeyī, why are you so deeply distressed?

Kaikeyī: Mother, because of my great misfortune and lack of merit, all the world speaks thus of my low character—that I, the mother of my dear sons, was the cause of their exile through Mantharā. Therefore, how can I even look upon the faces of my dear sons?
Arundhatī: My child, enough of this groundless suspicion of scandal. This matter was perceived directly by the noble gentlemen themselves through their inner vision at that very moment.
All of them: How so?
Arundhatī: This was done at the word of Mālyavat by Śūrpaṇakhā, who had assumed the form of Mantharā.
All: Alas! What wickedness is this on the part of the Rākṣasas, that they harass even defenseless women staying within their own homes!
Vasiṣṭha: Hum! Enough, enough with these trivialities at this auspicious moment; what further talk can there be of the threat from the Rākṣasa even now?
Rāma:
(Looking at Vasiṣṭha; with joy) This is that venerable son of Mitrāvaruṇa, by the sight of whom my mind becomes strangely melted with emotion.
Just as a moonstone [melts] from the light of the full moon. //34//
(To Lakṣmaṇa: Child, this way, this way!
Both:
(Approaching) Venerable family preceptor, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa salute you.
Vasiṣṭha said:
"O two calves, at their respective times, may your eyes attain the threefold refinement, being preceded by policy, righteousness, and knowledge. (35)
(Both pay homage to Arundhatī. Arundhatī: May you both be united with what is desired.
(Both, in turn, pay homage to all the Mothers.
All:
(Embracing them both tightly and smelling their heads: May that which we desire come to pass for you.
(Sītā approaches and bows to Vasiṣṭha. Vasiṣṭha: Child, may you give birth to heroes!
(Sītā bows to Arundhatī. Arundhatī:
(Embracing Sītā tightly.)
"O Jānakī, let these three—Lopāmudrā, Anasūyā, and I—and you yourself, all four devoted wives, now dwell here together with you. (36)
(Sītā: "My mother-in-law greets you. All: "Child, may you be the mother of a son who will establish the lineage!"
(Offstage: Let the citizens proceed with the festive rites today in every house; furthermore, let the officials apply themselves diligently to their respective duties.
O best of the twice-born, prepare once more the materials as prescribed. Thus does Kuśikapati, the disciple of Kṛśāśva, command you. (37)
Vasiṣṭha:
(Listening) Oh, how great is the power of my dear child’s fortune, that the venerable Kauśika has himself arrived to consecrate him upon the throne!
The others are dear, very dear to us.
(Then enters Viśvāmitra with his disciple. Viśvāmitra:

To pacify any obstacles to the sacrificial session, I have drawn this [child] from the hand of Daśaratha; whatever I have deliberated within my heart, and whatever agitation there was regarding the performance of the corresponding rites—[all that has been accomplished].

Today, through the favor of destiny and by means of our efforts and resources, having consecrated Śrī Rāma in the kingdom, we rejoice within ourselves again and again that the fruit has ripened for those who have attained peace. //38//
(Thus he walks around. Vasiṣṭha: This is that Kauśika, whose innate kṣatriya splendor is surpassed by his brahmanic power.
What is not marvelous about that treasure of supramundane wonder? //39//
(Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra approach each other and pay their respects. Viśvāmitra: O venerable son of Mitra and Varuṇa, why is it still being awaited even now?
Vasiṣṭha: Let him be honored as is appropriate.
Viśvāmitra:
(Addressing the assembly of divine sages: Let the consecration of the noble Rāma be performed.
(The sages act as is appropriate. Behind the scenes, the sound of a drum is heard; everyone listens with astonishment. (Again, behind the scenes:
"Let the Apsarases dance; let the surface of the earth be sprinkled by the clouds!"
May the wish-fulfilling trees themselves spontaneously shower down a rain of flowers here.
(All observe the rain of flowers with astonishment.
Vasiṣṭha: How is it that the blessed Indra, the subduer of Pāka and guardian of the world, approves of the consecration of the noble Rāma?
(Rāma, having performed the auspicious consecration rites, approaches Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra: "I salute my two gurus."
Both:
O Rāmabhadra, garden of virtues! Honored by your brothers and by the foremost kings of the Ikṣvāku lineage, bear for a long time the burden that has been borne for so long. 41.
The others: "So be it."
(Thus they express their approval. Viśvāmitra: My dear Rāmabhadra!
Rāma: May my teachers give their command.
Viśvāmitra:
Let these two, Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa, whose festive joy has been fully experienced, depart;
and let the Puṣpaka chariot, which is easily accessible at will, return to the King of Kings himself.

(Rāma does so. Viśvāmitra: Child Rāmabhadra, you have fulfilled the heavy command of your preceptor; dharma has been protected by the destruction of the Rākṣasa, and the three worlds have had the disease of their minds cured.

The gods have achieved their purpose, and the kingdom has been regained along with his younger brothers, friends, and wives; what more remains to be done? Please tell us that which would be even greater for our welfare. //42//
Rāma: There is even more auspiciousness than this; nevertheless, by the grace of the feet of the Blessed One, let this also come to pass.

(The Benediction: May the kings, their weariness dispelled, protect this circle of the earth; may the rain-clouds pour down rain according to desire; and may the entire kingdom once again have its crops fully ripened, with all calamities cast away.

May the world always bestow delight; may poets compose verses through the grace of the worthy; and may even those possessed of great learning, having reflected upon the abundant joy found in the works of others, proceed with gladness. //43//
Viśvāmitra: So be it.
(Thus they all exit. //The Seventh Act//
Upra.
